question.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$, which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2 & =3 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ -(-1)+2(2) & =5 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.
$$
